subject: Data residency & region pinning follow-up  Acme Bank
thread_summary: Post-demo follow-up covering data residency, region pinning options, cross-region failover behavior, and backup retention. Tech questions looped to Aditya; next steps: technical deep-dive and procurement touchpoint.

Subject: RE: Demo recap - region pinning questions

Hi Samira / Liam,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today - great conversation. Quick recap and action items on region/data residency topics we discussed: 

- Goals you shared: keep all production inference and logs for EU customers in the EU region, US customers in the US region, and allow cross-region failover for disaster recovery with clear contractual limits.
- Questions you raised: how region pinning works at request-level vs account-level, where logs and audit trails are stored, and how backups/geo-redundancy are handled.

Short answers: Redwood supports region pinning at the workspace level and at a per-route request attribute. We keep production inference in the pinned region; we also offer a cross-region failover policy that can be configured to route to a secondary pinned region in the event of an outage. Logs and audit events can be configured to remain in the pinned region and/or forwarded to your KMS / SIEM endpoint. Backups of customer-managed artifacts (models, KV caches) are retained according to the backup policy and can be stored in the same region or exported to your S3 bucket in a region you specify.

I don't want to get ahead of the technical details here - looping in Aditya to confirm specifics and numbers (RPO/RTO, replication windows, and standby behavior).

Next steps:
1) Aditya - can you confirm the default RPO/RTO for region-pinned deployments and how backups are handled (replication frequency, snapshot retention)?
2) Samira - could you confirm the list of regions you need pinned for Phase 1 (US-EAST, EU-WEST, APAC-SE)?
3) I'll attach a short architecture diagram and our SOC2 snapshot for your policy team to review; happy to schedule a technical deep-dive next week.

Attachments: region-pinning-arch.png (diagram), redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf (SOC 2 snapshot, redact PII)

Best,

Thanks Vanessa - this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our security/privacy and infra teams: 

1) If we pin a workspace to EU-WEST, are application logs and audit trails guaranteed to remain in EU-WEST? Is there any scenario where logs would be replicated to the US (e.g., for monitoring, analytics)?

2) For cross-region failover, can we configure a manual failover only (no automatic redirect) for compliance reasons? If automatic failover is used, are PII-containing requests ever routed outside the pinned region?

3) Backups: we require daily snapshots with a 90-day retention window and AES-256 encryption; backups must be stored in the same region unless we explicitly request export to our controlled S3. Can Redwood support that?

4) For auditing, we'd prefer logs to be write-only (immutable) for a configurable retention period. Is that available?

If Aditya can confirm the behaviors and provide any latency/availability trade-offs for active-active vs active-passive pinning, that would be great.

Subject: RE: Data residency & region pinning follow-up - technical details

Hi Samira / team - quick answers below. Happy to jump on a call to walk through diagrams.

1) Logs & audit trails:
- For a workspace pinned to EU-WEST, all server-side application logs, audit events, and request-level metadata are stored in EU-WEST by default. We do not replicate logs to another region unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication.
- Monitoring/analytics agents that you opt into (e.g., global analytics export) will require explicit consent/config to send telemetry outside the region.
- We support pushing logs to your customer-managed S3/GCS endpoint in the same region via our secure push connector (TLS + customer-managed KMS).

2) Cross-region failover behavior:
- Manual failover: supported. You can configure a policy that requires a manual approval step in the console or via API before failing over. This meets compliance requirements where you don't want automatic routing outside the pinned region.
- Automatic failover: supported as an option (with configurable whitelist/blacklist of content types). If enabled, you can set rules to prevent requests flagged as PII from leaving the pinned region. Note: request-level classification of PII happens at the application layer; if you need deterministic guarantees we recommend preventing automatic failover for PII-sensitive routes and only using manual failover for them.

3) Backups & retention:
- Daily snapshots: yes - we support scheduled daily snapshots of models and KV caches.
- Retention: configurable; we can set retention to 90 days for your account.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; customer-managed keys via KMS supported.
- Storage: snapshots are stored in the same region by default. We can also export encrypted snapshots to your S3 in the same region on request.

4) Immutable/append-only logs:
- We support write-once append-only storage for audit logs (immutable buckets) with configurable retention windows and tamper-evident checksums.

RPO/RTO guidance (typical):
- Active-passive (region pinned primary, manual failover to secondary): RPO ~ 15 minutes (snapshot/replication cadence), RTO ~ 15-30 minutes for failover depending on warm standby and route propagation.
- Active-active (multi-region serving with synchronous replication for metadata): RPO ~ near-zero for inference metadata, but increases cost and complexity; RTO for regional outages is near-instant for routing but you must manage regulatory constraints for PII.

Trade-offs: active-active gives lowest latency and fastest failover but exposes data to multiple regions (not acceptable for strict data residency). Active-passive with manual failover and encrypted same-region backups is the common pattern for regulated banks.

If you want, I can produce a short tech note with the configuration we recommend for Acme (EU-only logs, manual failover, daily encrypted snapshots retained 90 days) - will include API snippets and expected billing/throughput considerations.
